<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **4** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json`, `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/retired-keys/18.ui__ObjectGridProps__resizableColumns.ts`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **9** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **138** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 713b0fa76dbb6c0f60472cbbefd7690eedb1286e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `60e9e03a3d51e898eeaa90f514205fea20de1f86` — the merge of head `38159d1362f38beff333f798c34530ad821598c1` into base `713b0fa76dbb6c0f60472cbbefd7690eedb1286e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 60e9e03a3d51e898eeaa90f514205fea20de1f86 && git checkout 60e9e03a3d51e898eeaa90f514205fea20de1f86
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 713b0fa76dbb6c0f60472cbbefd7690eedb1286e 38159d1362f38beff333f798c34530ad821598c1 && git checkout -B drift-repro 713b0fa76dbb6c0f60472cbbefd7690eedb1286e && git merge --no-ff 38159d1362f38beff333f798c34530ad821598c1

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 713b0fa76dbb6c0f60472cbbefd7690eedb1286e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 713b0fa76dbb6c0f60472cbbefd7690eedb1286e` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `52c4c42d72858f679b3348f8caede1da7e7e4b45`
Local-runs: none

Isolated contract reviewer for PR #21463 (card #21445), written at 2026-10-02T20:50Z. Inputs: the card body and its four comments (triage `5958164933`, claim `5958653004`, dev report `5960961904`, the seat's arm-A answer `5960993628`), the PR body, its 14-file list and the net diff `origin/main...52c4c42d72` (+1167 / −28), the head's check-runs, read-only objectui at the `.objectui-sha` pin `89cad75d55` and `origin/main`'s `packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts`. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

**The seven typed members of `ComponentPropsMap['object-grid']` (`ObjectGridPropsSchema`), each against the renderer's read at the pin.**

- `rowHeight` → `RowHeightSchema` by reference — **right.** `resolveRowHeightMode` (`ObjectGrid.tsx:1311`) admits a string only when `ROW_HEIGHT_TO_DENSITY_MODE` has it as an own key, and that table is `Record` keyed by the spec's `RowHeight` (`@object-ui/core` `normalize-list-view.ts:48`, five keys); anything else answers `compact`. The declared set and the honoured set are the same five values; no honoured value is refused.
- `rowColor` → `RowColorConfigSchema` by reference — **right.** `useRowColor` (`useRowColor.ts:72-90`) reads exactly `config.field` and `config.colors`, and returns nothing when either is absent; `field` required and `colors` optional is that read. No honoured value is refused.
- `navigation` → `NavigationConfigSchema` by reference — **right.** `useNavigationOverlay` reads `mode`, `size`, `width`, `openNewTab`, `preventNavigation` (plus the retired `view` only in its docblock); every one is declared on the carrier `object-kanban` / `object-calendar` / `object-timeline` already take (`component.zod.ts:4743`, `:4911`, `:6356` on `main`). No honoured value is refused.
- `conditionalFormatting` → `ListViewSchema.shape.conditionalFormatting` by reference — **right**, and by-reference is mandatory here since the rule shape is declared nowhere else. What the shared evaluator honours and this door now refuses: the two objectui-native spellings the dev named (`{ field, operator, value, backgroundColor, … }` and `{ expression, … }`) and, inside the first, the flat colour members `backgroundColor` / `textColor` / `borderColor` at rule level instead of `style`. The list view refuses them identically today, the tolerance is a consumer-side alias of the kind Prime Directive #12 forbids, and objectui#6152 carries the convergence. One correction to the dev's census sentence ("no bag writes either"): it holds for document bags; objectui's own grid tests at the pin do write the native dialect as host-mounted schemas (`plugin-grid/src/__tests__/gridRowDecorationMembers-8071.test.tsx:188-260`) — escalated below as an objectui follow-up item, not a spec defect.
- `bulkActionDefs` → `z.array(BulkActionDefSchema)` by identity — **right**; the pin asserts the same def the list view's element holds. The four gaps the dev reports are real at the pin and each stands on the list view's door by construction, because it is the same schema: `actionDef` is renderer-attached and refused by guidance on purpose (`bulk-action.zod.ts:344`); undeclared `params[]` widget keys that `bulkParamToField` spreads are refused by `BULK_PARAM_WIDGET_CONFIG_KEYS` under its recorded ruling (`:156`, `:228`); `visible` takes a string or the `{ dialect, source }` envelope whose `dialect` is required (`EvaluatedExpressionInputSchema`), while objectui's `ExpressionWire` makes `dialect` optional; `params[].type` is `FieldType` (`:248`) while the twin types it `string`. Leaving all four alone is right under triage's "report the gap and do not widen it silently": the first two are deliberate refusals already ruled, the last two are the objectui twin being wider than the spec, which is a mirror-parity matter for objectui, not a spec gap. They are NOT on the dev's objectui#6152 follow-up list; escalated below.
- `aggregations` → `[{ field, type: AggregationFunction }]`, strict, module-private — **right.** `useGroupedData.ts:17-22` declares `AggregationConfig { field: string; type: AggregationType }` and nothing else, `useServerGrouping.ts:79` compiles the same two members, and `AggregationType` is the six values of `AggregationFunction` (the pin asserts the exact set). `ListViewSchema` has no `aggregations` member, so there is nothing to reference; no export is added, so `api-surface` is untouched. No honoured value is refused.
- `operations` → strict `{ create?, update?, delete?, export? }` with `read` / `import` refused by guidance — **right as arm A** (seat answer `5960993628`). Reads at the pin: the replace-not-merge default (`:1818-1822`), `update` / `delete` (`:1898-1899`, `:4485`), `export` (`:4088`, `:5340`, `:6141`), `create` (`:5468`); a grep of `plugin-grid/src` for `operations.read` / `operations.import` finds no read. The one refused writer is objectui's `README.md:226` (ruled A). One more objectui-side fact for the follow-up: `ObjectView` composes the grid node's `operations` as `{ ...operations, create: false }` (`plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx:1586`, `:2485`) and reads `operations.read` itself (`:1720`), so a view that authors `read` lands it on the composed grid node; that matters once objectui's strict face judges composed nodes against this row.

**`resizableColumns` retired.** Route and kit checked against `spec-property-retirement/SKILL.md` on `origin/main`:

- Tombstone: `retiredKey()` on a strict shape is the right route (§2 row 1); the guidance string keeps the five house conventions (fully qualified key in the `object-grid` property form the `defaultSort` tombstone uses; "was removed in @objectstack/spec 17.7.0 (ADR-0049)", 17.7.0 being the minor this `minor` changeset cuts from 17.6.0; the dash clause; "Use `resizable`. Rename the key; the value (a boolean) is unchanged."; the `os migrate meta --from 17` sentence). Both channels are pinned (`tsc` via a consumed `@ts-expect-error`, the parse via the prescription regex).
- D2 conversion `object-grid-resizable-columns-removed`: protocol 18, `retiredFromLoadPath: true`, `retiredAfter: '17.6.0'` = `packages/spec/package.json` (the census pin's rule), inserted at its identifier's sort position in `MAJOR_18_CONVERSIONS` with `order: 57` = highest + 1, scoped by `component.type === 'object-grid'`. Every arm matches the renderer's `schema.resizable ?? schema.resizableColumns ?? true`: `resizable` set → the legacy key strips as a lossless delete (`resizable` wins, as `??` says); `resizableColumns` alone → renamed with its value unchanged, so `resizableColumns: false` alone becomes `resizable: false` and keeps defeating the renderer's `?? true` default; both set and disagreeing → `resizable` wins and the legacy value is discarded, exactly the `??`, with the discarded value named for the author in the D3 `reason`; `resizable: null` → `??` reads through null, and the rename overwrites it. Idempotent by construction (the key is gone after either arm). The fixture's four notices are three renames (region, nested `page:card.children`, slotted) and one strip; the kanban sibling and the keyless grid are untouched; the emitted path follows the `defaultSort` precedent (destination path).
- `RETIRED_KEYS_BY_MAJOR[18]` row `ui/ObjectGridProps:resizableColumns` from the entries file `18.ui__ObjectGridProps__resizableColumns.ts` (the `defaultSort` naming), generated into `registry.ts`, spelled as the `authorable-surface/ui.json` line minus `[RETIRED]`.
- D3: `object-grid-resizable-columns-retired` (one per retirement family, carrying `conversionIds`) and `ui-object-grid-row-members-typed` (a narrowing with no conversion, the `ui-object-grid-export-options-closed` precedent) — both with non-empty `reason` and `acceptanceCriteria`, inserted at their ids' sort positions.
- Two `STEP18_RATIONALE` fragments at orders 62 and 63 = highest (61) + 1 and + 2, at their ids' sort positions. The pre-existing duplicate orders 56 / 60 (rationale) and 55 (conversions) are on `main`, not this PR's, and the sort breaks ties by id.
- Nothing missing, nothing doubled: no `packages/spec/liveness/` ledger covers component props (zero rows for `ObjectGridProps` or `resizableColumns` on `main`), so no ledger row is owed and `Spec property liveness` is green; no form input, i18n label or skill names the key; `content/docs` carried it only in the regenerated reference row, now `never` / `[REMOVED]`. `authorable-surface.base.json` still spells the key by design (a pinned anchor at `baseRev`, never the live surface). The repo-root `sdui.manifest.json` description still says "the deprecated `resizableColumns` is only read when this is absent" because it mirrors objectui's registry text at the pin (`plugin-grid/src/index.tsx:265`); it refreshes with the pin bump — one more line for the objectui follow-up.
- Absence pin: tree-scoped, over exactly the radius `turbo.json` declares for `@objectstack/spec#test:repo` (`packages/**` by extension, `examples/**` json / md / yaml plus `examples/*/src/**/*.ts`, `content/**`, `skills/**`, `scripts/**`), registered in `vitest.repo-tests.json`, exclusions structural (the kit, release prose, gitignored build output), no allowlist file. Right.

**The census, re-checked.** objectstack `origin/main`: the two showcase grids (`my-work.page.ts`, `command-center.page.ts`) write `columns`, `filter`, `objectName`, `title`, `width` and none of the seven; the `conditionalFormatting` / `bulkActionDefs` / `rowColor` / `userActions.rowHeight` hits in `examples/app-showcase/src/ui/views/*.view.ts` are list-view members judged by `ListViewSchema`, unaffected; `packages/platform-objects` writes none; zero `resizableColumns` writers. objectui at the pin: the one refused writer is `README.md:226` (`operations.read`); `rowHeight: 40` hits are view-config overlays (`updateViewConfig`), not grid bags; `navigation: 'drawer'` is a timeline diagnostics test; `resizableColumns: false` in `ObjectView.tableSlotRelay-10976.test.tsx:250` is a WITHHELD-key probe asserting the key never reaches the grid node, not a writer. The census stands, with the grid-test note above.

**Generated artifacts.**

- `content/docs/references/ui/component.mdx`: the seven rows and the new nested shapes (`aggregations[number]`, `conditionalFormatting[number]`, `rowColor`, `bulkActionDefs[number]`, `navigation`, `operations`) render the schema; the `resizableColumns` row is `never` with the `[REMOVED]` prescription. Caused by this diff and right. Two further moves are generator-caused and the dev names only one: `ObjectGridProps.grouping.fields[]` now renders `order?` / `collapsed?`, AND `ObjectGridProps.data[provider='api'].read` / `.write` now render `method?` — the input face of defaulted fields — while the identical shared defs on sibling rows on the same page (`ObjectKanbanProps.grouping`, `ObjectGanttProps` / `ObjectMapProps` / `ObjectTreeProps.data[provider='api']`) still render `order` / `method` (counts `main` → branch: `method?:` 0 → 2, `order?:` 0 → 1, `collapsed?:` 0 → 1). Both faces describe one schema and `check:generated` is green (Lint & Repo Gates), so the artifact is right as output; the page is now internally inconsistent, which is a generator determinism defect this diff's evaluation order (the `ListViewSchema` import and `.shape` access) exposed. Escalated below.
- `authorable-surface/ui.json`: one line gains `[RETIRED]`; the surface lists top-level keys only, so the typed members add no rows. Right.
- `docs/audits/2026-07-unknown-key-strictness-ledger.counts/ui.md`: +2 strict sites (`GridAggregationSchema`, `GridOperationsSchema`), 188 → 190 and `component.zod.ts` 58 → 60. Right.
- `dropped-refinements.baseline.json`: `ui/ObjectGridProps` gains `bulkActionDefs.element`, 652 → 653 — it is `ui/ListView`'s existing `bulkActionDefs.element` site reaching the grid door by identity; `conditionalFormatting` adds no site because the list view has none for it either. Right.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/spec` `minor` with the BREAKING banner, under the launch-window convention `check-changeset-no-major` enforces (Check Changeset green). **`Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` is the right arm.** The dispatch's `no (narrowing)` predated the measurement; `check-widening-tells.mjs:1584-1589` names one shape that is a true refusal although it only narrows — "a member bounded inside a bag that was a universal acceptor (`z.unknown()` / `z.any()`)" — with the remedy "declare `Clause-②: yes` and route it to at-tier review", and `aggregations[].field` / `.type` and the four `operations` toggles are exactly that shape. `yes` takes at least `minor`; `(narrowing)` is BREAKING and the banner is present. The seat accepted the switch in `5960993628`.

Changeset, sentence by sentence: the `!` title; the `Clause-②` line; exactly one ADR-0087 marker, `registered`, naming the three ids, all new in this diff (the gate's rule: every id resolves at HEAD and at least one is new); the BREAKING paragraph is factual — the row is read by the component-props gate (`packages/lint/src/validate-component-props.ts`) on `objectstack validate` / `build` / `lint`, and a page component's `properties` is `z.record(z.string(), z.unknown())` on the load path (`page.zod.ts:324`), so a stored page still saves and loads; the seven member bullets match ①; "`ObjectGridProps` (and `ObjectGridPropsParsed`) … `resizableColumns` is `never`" matches the exports at `:4122` / `:4130` and pin §4; every FROM → TO row is right, including "`resizableColumns: true` beside `resizable: false` → `resizable: false`" (the `??`) and `rowHeight: 'comfortable'` being a density name, not a spec value; the one-line fix is right; the retirement-kit paragraph matches the registries; the census paragraph matches the re-check; "Deployed metadata was not measured" is the honest bound. PR body lines one and two are `Fixes #21445` and `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, matching the changeset.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev deviations:

1. **Arm `yes (narrowing)` instead of the dispatched `no (narrowing)`** — answered in ②: measured, honest, accepted by the seat.
2. **`operations` narrowed to the four read members (arm A).** The seat answered A in `5960993628`; the measurement holds (no reader of `read` / `import` in `plugin-grid/src`). Carried to objectui#6152: the README line, the twin's two members, and the `ObjectView` relay fact in ①.
3. **`Fixes #21445` kept** — the seat did not route the card to the decision inbox; "The card this PR closes must claim this branch" and "Part-of PR must not also close its card" are green. No action.
4. **Five `repo`-project files NOT MEASURED locally** (`build-schemas-check-mode`, `dist-freshness`, `dist-freshness-adoption`, `publish-smoke-boot-failure`, `publish-smoke-port-collision`) — measured by the `Test Core (1/6)` … `(6/6)` check-runs, which run `pnpm turbo run test test:repo` (`ci.yml:826`) and so `@objectstack/spec#test:repo` = `vitest run --project repo`. At the final read of the head's check-runs (2026-10-02T20:49:38Z) all six shards had concluded `success`, so the five files are measured, and the whole roster stood at 33 `success` and 2 `skipped` by design (`Console Pin Gate`, `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`), with nothing failed and nothing still running.
5. **Plain `git merge` of `origin/main` `086ad0aa68`** — that commit touched `.changeset/21426-native-number-comparand.md` and two `packages/service-analytics` files only; no generated artifact, so no `os-regen-merge` was owed. Right.

`out_of_scope_findings`, each as a reading escalated to the seat:

1. **`check-widening-tells` T2 fires on import specifiers.** Confirmed a matcher false positive by the gate's own definition (T2 is a member of `z.enum` / `z.union` / `z.discriminatedUnion` / an `as const` array; `import { … }` specifiers are none). It moved nothing here because T1 forced `yes`. The gate's own remedy text says to repair the matcher with a `--self-test` case or file that repair as its own card; the dev's finding is class a with a named repro — escalated to the seat to file.
2. **Sibling rows still `z.unknown()`.** Confirmed on `main`: `object-kanban.conditionalFormatting` (`:4670`), `navigation` on `object-map` (`:5502`), `object-gantt` (`:5715`), `object-tree` (`:6040`). Escalated to the family's closure card.
3. **objectui#6152 follow-up list.** Confirmed as the dev lists it; the seat should add: the two twin-wider `bulkActionDefs` gaps (`visible.dialect` optional, `params[].type: string`); the `ObjectView` → grid relay of `operations` whole (`ObjectView.tsx:2485`) beside its own `operations.read` read (`:1720`); the grid tests that write the native `conditionalFormatting` dialect (`gridRowDecorationMembers-8071.test.tsx`); and the `index.tsx:265` registry description that still names the deprecated `resizableColumns` (mirrored into this repo's `sdui.manifest.json`).
4. **The `grouping.fields[]` rendering.** Wider than reported (the `method?` move too) and inconsistent across sibling rows on one page — a generator determinism defect with a named repro (this diff). Escalated to the seat to file; not a contract face and not a FAIL reason.
